limits: No alternative implementation or benchmark executed; no language or scheduler performance ranking.
No network identity, execution authority, physical, hard-real-time, MLS/CNSA, availability or whole-lane qualification.
component: Direct pinned federation and inbox-delivery conformance
constraints: Offline immutable canonical snapshot, at most 65536 bytes/depth eight and sixteen peers. Validate every row; selected peer must pin exact policy bytes and permit issuer and every signed capability.
Caller-authenticated snapshot/task pins and independent trusted time/revision floors. Revalidate bundle; earliest expiry wins. No transitive lookup or rule language.
No supplied target memory budget, throughput SLA or hard deadline. Four local delivery traces exercise two distinct caller clock domains, not a deployed transport.
alternatives: Closed table in Python using lexical JSON hooks and versioned public bundle verification.
Rust/Serde or C#/F# token reader with a conformant closed-table adapter.
Erlang/Elixir OTP JSON callbacks and immutable binaries.
Cedar scoped authorization policies or OPA/Rego declarative document queries when a general policy language is actually required.
rationale: KEEP after fresh runtime, contract and twelve federation methods plus four real-API delivery traces. Exact direct-peer membership and complete scope predicates are explicit and bounded; no new mismatch found.

Cedar and Rego are serious policy technologies, but introducing a policy language does not improve this closed direct-match profile or authenticate snapshot provisioning. Typed alternative runtimes can implement it; none demonstrated a material advantage under current constraints.

A controlled removal of the selected peer policy-pin comparison is detected by an existing assertion. Negative traces retain the fact that stale supplied configuration can still authenticate and closing the inbox cannot revoke an already returned copy.
